maxRps.rationale: Prose gives no explicit admission ceiling, so use a large typical default well above the stated 3,000 rps normal load.

instances.rationale: Prose states 15 instances of the search service.

concurrencyPerInstance.rationale: No concurrency figure given; assume a typical moderate concurrency per instance for a service doing query parsing/ranking plus a downstream call.

serviceTimeMs.rationale: No explicit CPU time given for parsing/ranking; assume a modest value typical of in-process query parsing and result ranking excluding the Elasticsearch call.

hitRate.rationale: Prose states hit rates are much lower than typical because search queries are diverse; assume a low hit rate reflecting this.

hitLatencyMs.rationale: No round-trip figure given; assume a typical remote cache network round-trip time.

cpuTimeMs.rationale: No figure given; typical in-memory cache server processing time is sub-millisecond, orders of magnitude below hit latency.

ttlSeconds.rationale: Prose states search results are cached for 30 seconds.

keyspaceHotSet.rationale: Prose implies a diverse, low-repeat query space (few hot keys) since most searches are for things nobody searched for recently.

connectionPoolSize.rationale: Prose states a client-side connection pool of 50 connections to Elasticsearch.

queryTimeMs.rationale: No explicit query time given; assume a typical full-text search query latency for Elasticsearch under moderate load.

writeRatio.rationale: Prose states indexing happens on a completely separate pipeline that doesn't touch this read path, so this path is effectively all reads.

readReplicas.rationale: Prose explicitly states no Elasticsearch replicas are run for search traffic.

replicaApplyRate.rationale: No replicas exist for this read path, so replica apply rate is zero.
